thread.title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (NVDA, DIS, ROKU, DBX)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (NVDA, DIS, ROKU, DBX)
text:
Shutterstock photo Equities moved higher on Friday, driven by the jobs report for April. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 332 points, or 1.39% to break back above 24,000, while the S&P 500 Index added 1.28%. Thanks to a 4% gain in Apple ( AAPL ), which surged to all-time highs, the Nasdaq was the big winner, adding 121 points, or 1.7%.
Traders continue to focus on positive Q1 earnings to keep this momentum going and to, hopefully, propel stocks out of the range-bound movement they’ve been in over the past two months. In that vein, here are four stocks to keep an eye on.
Nvidia ( NVDA ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, May 8.
Wall Street expects Nvidia to earn $1.45 per share on revenue of $2.89 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 79 cents per share on revenue of $1.94 billion.
What to Watch: Shares of the graphic chip powerhouse rose 5.62% last week, reversing the pressure they’ve been under amid the broader tech selloff. Analysts expect EPS to jump 84%, while sales are seen rising 49%. The company has dominated graphics processors in data centers and the to the extent those prospects, along with artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency mining remains strong, Nvidia stock should exceed its all-time high of $254 following the report.
Disney ( DIS ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, May 8.
Wall Street expects Disney to earn $1.69 per share on revenue of $14.08 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to $1.50 per share on revenue of $13.34 billion.
What to Watch: The media and entertainment behemoth just unveiled its ESPN Plus streaming platform to little-to-no fanfare. The stock has fallen about 7% since the company reported first quarter earnings. Nevertheless, this quarter’s report will be important as it will serve as a gauge for Disney’s ambitions to compete with Netflix ( NFLX ) as a full over-the-top (OTT) streaming platform. Early reports suggests Disney’s OTT pricing plan may seek to undercut Netflix. Will it announce anything to support those rumors?
Roku ( ROKU ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, May 9.
Wall Street expects Roku to lose 15 cents per share on revenue of $127.15 million. This will be the company’s third earnings report as a public issue.
What to Watch: Describing itself as a "content distribution platform,” Roku has ambitions of becoming the go-to platform for TV streaming. To realize that goal, however, it has to take on behemoths such as Amazon’s ( AMZN ) Fire Stick, Google’s ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Chromecast and Apple’s Apple TV. On Wednesday analyst will press CEO Anthony Wood about the company’s money-making capabilities as it faces these incumbent tech heavyweights.
Dropbox ( DBX ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, May 10.
Wall Street expects Dropbox to earn 4 cents per share on revenue of $309.26 million.
What to Watch: This will be the tech company’s first earnings report as a public issue. Dropbox, which makes money by selling cloud subscriptions to their product, has over 500 million registered users, spanning 180 countries, according to its Form-S1 filed with the SEC. 100 million of those users were added 2017 alone, representing a 25% jump year over year. But of the 500 million users, just 11 million or 2.2% are paying for the service. This means 97.8% of its client base remains untapped. In other words, beyond the top- and bottom line numbers, analysts will focus on the strength of its user base to better gauge the extent of the company’s long-term profit capabilities.
